title: Suspense
paragraphs: CBS's landmark thriller anthology, presenting murder, psychological suspense, crime, horror, and the supernatural with major radio and Hollywood performers in standalone dramatic stories.
CBS mystery/thriller anthology known as radio’s outstanding theater of thrills. Frozen GRH snapshot contains one 1948 episode and 102 episodes from 1957-58, all with accepted structured matches.

GRH documents the program through CBS anthology run (June 17, 1942 to September 30, 1962) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and William N. Robson Hollywood era (November 4, 1956 to August 23, 1959) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are William N. Robson (producer on 99 recordings, director on 97 recordings, host on 36 recordings, writer on 10 recordings, radio adaptor on 6 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), George Walsh (announcer on 92 recordings), Jack Kruschen (performer on 24 recordings), Joe DeSantis (performer on 21 recordings), Ellen Morgan (performer on 18 recordings), Barney Phillips (performer on 17 recordings), and Sam Pierce (performer on 15 recordings, writer on 2 recordings, and radio adaptor on 1 recording).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and violent crime, madness and psychological instability, isolation and entrapment, war and military conflict, science and speculative danger, and deception and hidden identity.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Celebrity-driven dramatic anthology, Literary and original-story adaptation tradition, and Late Golden Age network drama.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|escape|Escape]] (108 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (92 shared credited people), [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (90 shared credited people), [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]] (80 shared credited people), and [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (60 shared credited people).
